title: Ablative Absolute
description: A subordinate clause construction grammatically detached from the main clause. It provides adverbial context such as time, cause, condition, or concession.

examples.translation: The city having been captured (When the city was captured), the soldiers departed.
Caesar being leader (With Caesar as leader), we fear nothing.
As the sun was rising, they set sail.

mnemonic: Look for two ablatives in a row separated by commas near sentence starts.

title: Special Deponent Verbs + Ablative
description: These five deponents take their direct complement in the Ablative case instead of the Accusative due to their original middle/reflexive meaning ('to benefit oneself with').

examples.translation: Glabrio uses a sword (literally: 'serves himself with a sword').

title: Prepositions with Dual Cases (in, sub)
description: Governing Accusative when indicating movement toward a target, or Ablative when indicating location, state, or position at rest.
